 Pakistan's pacers rattle Sri Lanka top order in second Test
 Abbas and Razaullah take two wickets each while Saqib Khan claim one wicket to destroy the visitors in Pindi
 Sports Desk 
 November 17, 2026 
 3 min read

 Photo: PCB 
 Sri Lanka on Tuesday had a disappointing start as they reached 52-5 in the first innings in their second Test against Pakistan at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi.
 Kusal Mendis, the skipper, and Sonal Dinusha were batting. 
Saqib Khan, who had ripped through Sri Lanka's batting in the first Test, provided an early breakthrough when he had Pasindu Sooriyabandara for just two when he edged a delivery pitched outside the off-stumps to keeper Ghazi Ghori.
Soon afterwards seasoned pacer Mohammad Abbas got rid of Dinesh Chandimal (7) to leave the visitors reeling at 16-2. Dinesh hit one four from 13 balls.
Abbas struck again when he sent Kamindu Mendis for seven to leave Sri Lanka gasping at 25-3. Mendis hit one four. And in the next over Razaullah, who had a bad first Test, added to the miseries of Sri Lanka when he dislodged Lahiru Udara for four.
 And Razaullah looked too dangerous and he this time got a crucial wicket of inform de Silva (1), trapped lbw to leave the visitors in deep trouble. 
Abbas and Razaullah got two wickets each while Saqib Khan claimed one wicket.
Earlier Pakistan won the toss and elected to field in order to exploit early moisture.
The hosts made one change to their playing XI, bringing in all-rounder Aamer Jamal in place of Arafat Minhas.
Sri Lanka also made a change, recalling left-arm spinner Prabath Jayasuriya to strengthen their bowling attack.
The five-day match, which runs from November 17 to 21, is the series decider after the opening Test ended in a draw.
Pakistan captain Babar Azam opted to bowl first on a surface that appeared to offer assistance to seamers during the opening stages, with moisture remaining underneath a substantial covering of grass.
Conditions were cool and sunny in Rawalpindi, with temperatures around 12 degrees Celsius at the start of play.
Pakistan will be looking to build on the performances of Saud Shakeel and debutant Saqib Khan in the opening Test. Shakeel scored 93 and 97 in two disciplined innings, while Saqib claimed seven wickets for 130 runs on debut to earn the player-of-the-match award.
Babar, meanwhile, made 50 and 34 in the first Test but remains without a Test century for nearly four years, having gone 42 innings without reaching three figures.
Sri Lanka will draw confidence from the batting performances of Dhananjaya de Silva and captain Kusal Mendis in the opening match.
De Silva struck 167, while Mendis scored 119 as the pair shared a decisive 249-run partnership after Sri Lanka had slipped to 65 for three.
Sonal Dinusha has also been a consistent performer for Sri Lanka, scoring 615 runs in five Tests this year, and will be among the players Pakistan will need to contain.
The visitors have brought back Jayasuriya, whose record against Pakistan makes him an important addition. He has taken 26 wickets in four Tests against the hosts at an average of 31.12, including two five-wicket hauls.
In the drawn opening Test
Pakistan declared their first innings at 434 for nine, but Sri Lanka responded strongly with 446, securing a 12-run first-innings lead.
Pakistan were 284 for eight in their second innings when the captains agreed to a draw, with approximately 141 overs lost during the match because of rain and poor light.
The result left the two-match series level at 0-0, setting up Tuesday's contest as a straight shootout for the series.
Both teams have struggled in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle, with Sri Lanka sitting seventh and Pakistan ninth in the standings before the second Test. A positive result will therefore be important for both sides as they seek to improve their positions.
Squads
 Pakistan
Babar Azam (captain), Azan Awais, Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, Saud Shakeel, Salman Ali Agha, Ghazi Ghori (wicketkeeper), Aamer Jamal, Razaullah, Mohammad Abbas, Saqib Khan, Arafat Minhas.
 Sri Lanka
Kusal Mendis (captain and wicketkeeper), Lahiru Udara, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva, Sonal Dinusha, Milan Rathnayake, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando.
